title: Concrete Pump Hopper Capacity vs Output (m³/h)
seoTitle: Concrete Pump Hopper Capacity | Pinjin Catalogue
description: Hopper litres are not pumping output. Xingtai tables list 0.1–0.7 m³ hoppers beside separate m³/h rows. Mixer-pump 400/500 series notes are mixing drums, not the 0.4 m³ pump hopper.

relatedPaths.label: Concrete pump output m³/h catalogue rows

answerBlock.what: Hopper capacity is the receiving volume on the pump, printed in m³. It is not theoretical output. Pinjin electric/diesel tables list hoppers from 0.1 m³ (Electric 10 series) through 0.25–0.4 m³ on compact and mid trailers to 0.7 m³ on Electric 60 / Electric 80. The integrated mixer pump lists a 0.4 m³ hopper plus a separate series note: 30 series with 400 mixer; 40/50 series with 500 mixer.
answerBlock.who: Buyers who saw ‘hopper 0.6 m³’ on a marketplace listing and need to match a Xingtai row without treating hopper litres as m³/h.
factors: Printed hopper m³ on the model page
Separate output m³/h row
Mixer-pump drum series note versus pump hopper
ACPA: do not work in the hopper unless the unit is shut down and accumulator pressure is zero

faqs.question: Is hopper capacity the same as pumping output?
faqs.answer: No. Electric 20 lists hopper 0.25 m³ and output 8–10 m³/h. Electric 80 lists hopper 0.7 m³ and output 60 m³/h. Use both printed rows. Hopper volume is a buffer at the grate, not cubic metres placed per hour.

faqs.question: What hopper sizes does Pinjin publish?
faqs.answer: Catalogue examples: Electric 10 series 0.1 m³; Tractor-Driven 4100 0.25 m³; Electric 20 0.25 m³; Electric 30 / Low Pressure 40 / Diesel 30 0.3 m³; Electric 40 / 50 / mixer pump / Diesel 40–60 0.4 m³; Low Pressure 60 0.5 m³; LZ-80 / Diesel 120 0.6 m³; Electric 60 and Electric 80 0.7 m³. Missing cells on other pages stay blank.

faqs.question: Is the mixer-pump ‘400/500 mixer’ the hopper?
faqs.answer: No. The integrated mixer pump lists hopper 0.4 m³ and a series note: 30 series with 400 mixer; 40/50 series with 500 mixer. That note is the mixing drum pairing, not a second hopper litre figure. The unit is still a trailer that mixes and pumps — not a batching plant.
